entities.summary:
Sudines was a Babylonian sage and mathematician who lived in the 3rd century BCE. He is mentioned as one of the famous Chaldean mathematicians and astronomers by later Roman writers like Strabo.

Sudines was a prominent figure in the Babylonian intellectual scene, known for his contributions to the fields of mathematics, astronomy, and astrology. He is believed to have written several treatises on these subjects, which were later translated into Greek and Latin.

Despite his significant contributions to the development of Babylonian mathematics and astronomy, Sudines' legacy was largely forgotten until recent years, when scholars began to rediscover his works and reevaluate his importance in the history of science.

One striking example of Sudines' influence is the influence of his astronomical models on later Greek astronomers, such as Hipparchus and Ptolemy. His work on the movements of the planets and the stars helped shape the understanding of the solar system for centuries to come.
